_source: Scope text quoted from EP 6.49 (the ratified cohort recommendation, discuss.ens.domains/t/22237). Milestones are NOT yet recorded: they come from Award Notice Item 5 (KPIs and reporting metrics), which is not yet in the committee workspace. Empty milestone lists are honest, not placeholder — the 80% completion metric is undefined until they land.
_epoch_note: Reports are due within 30 days of each calendar quarter end (Program Terms clause 6.3). The public ENS Forum version is contractual, not a courtesy.

namespace.scope: ENSv2 migration of their on-chain subname stack, continued maintenance of existing tooling, and business development.
namespace.why_funded: One of the ecosystem's primary subname infrastructure teams: SDKs, APIs, CCIP gateways, and custom deployments including Celo, Filecoin and Rootstock. The award reflects the counterfactual: no comparable subname infrastructure exists at this scale, and the ENSv2 transition makes that work time-critical.
namespace.watch: SPP2 subname issuance exceeded target by more than an order of magnitude, but the committee noted that figure is concentrated in a small number of large deployments.
namespace.external_note: EP 6.49: key milestones depend on ENSv2 shipping to mainnet, and the committee accounted for this in the negotiated milestone structure. A slip here is not a delivery failure.

goldsky.scope: Operate ENS indexing as a dedicated public service, at the expanded scope presented as Option B in their application.
goldsky.why_funded: Indexing is a shared dependency consumed across the ecosystem and had previously been funded inside larger provider scopes. The committee's judgment is that a dependency of this weight is best held as a standalone mandate: one accountable owner, priced on its own merits.
goldsky.watch: New to the SPP and evaluated accordingly. Selection was conditioned on explicit commitment to the full Option B scope.

unruggable.scope: Continued gateway operation, extending into developer tooling and interoperability R&D.
unruggable.why_funded: Gateway infrastructure powering cross-chain resolution in production, including base.eth and ENSIP-19 reverse resolution. Funded at the full ask on the strength of shipped, verifiable protocol infrastructure that ENS depends on today, and a delivery record with no abandoned commitments.
unruggable.watch: Award unchanged from SPP2 at $400,000, so the stream was never modified at the cohort switch and has run continuously since 12 September 2025.

fluidkey.scope: Privacy-preserving ENS infrastructure: an ENSIP, wallet-agnostic contracts, and a resolver kit designed to be maintained independently of Fluidkey's own product.
fluidkey.why_funded: The smallest award in the cohort, treated by the committee as a deliberate position on an underdeveloped capability. The proposal cleanly separates the public-goods layer from the company's commercial product, budgets an audit, and self-funds its own reference integration.
fluidkey.watch: Registration upside is less proven than elsewhere in the cohort; the cost is priced accordingly.
